title: Knowledge Digester: the owner's curated skill list skips the sign-off and the budget
requested_outcome: Context: the Knowledge Digester (app/digest/; docs/product-memory/KNOWLEDGE_DIGESTER_V1.md and SOURCE_ASSIMILATION_V1.md on the trunk) proposes what CLIVE should take from an external artifact. app/digest/propose.py keeps at most BUDGET proposals per target (5 builder skills, best first; the rest are held back) and gives every builder_skill proposal a needs_owner reason (see _group_plan). The owner decided on 30 September (docs/product-memory/OWNER_DECISIONS_2026-09-30.md, 'The owner's curated skill list is the owner's decision'): a skill on a list the owner supplies needs no further owner sign-off and does not count against a proposal budget; everything else stays as it is. Build an explicit curated mode, off by default, that does exactly that and nothing more. (1) app/digest/propose.py: the function that makes proposals gains a keyword curated: bool = False. When true, builder_skill proposals are not budgeted (every one is kept, best first, and none is counted as held back) and carry no needs_owner reason; their explanation says the owner listed this artifact's skills himself (OWNER_DECISIONS_2026-09-30). Every other target (tool_connector, review_check, design_system, native_objective, product_memory, reference_only, rejected) keeps its budget and its needs_owner exactly as now. A licence that forbids reuse, or no licence, still makes a proposal need the owner, curated or not (the licence path is unchanged), and nothing about credentials or secret places changes. (2) app/digest/pipeline.py: digest(...) gains curated: bool = False and passes it to proposing; nothing else in the pipeline changes, and the store's records and schema do not change. (3) scripts/digest.py and scripts/digest_intake.py: a --curated flag (help: 'the owner listed this artifact's skills himself: no sign-off and no budget for its builder skills (OWNER_DECISIONS_2026-09-30)') passed through; the printed one-line summary says 'curated' when it is set; --curated with --self or with --no-relate is refused as a bad argument (exit 1), like the others. (4) app/digest/report.py: when curated, the Proposals section says in one sentence that the owner listed this artifact's skills himself, and the 'held back by the budget' line names only targets that were budgeted. Tests in a new file tests/test_digest_curated.py, built the way tests/test_digest_propose.py builds its units and self-model: an artifact with seven skill folders (each a SKILL.md with front matter and a few steps) proposes at most five builder skills, each needing the owner, without curated, and all seven, none needing the owner, with curated; in the same artifact a proposal for another target (a remote API connector or a design token set) keeps its budget and still needs the owner under curated; a skill folder whose licence forbids reuse still needs the owner under curated; digest(..., curated=True) passes it through; the scripts' --curated flag works and is refused with --self and with --no-relate. Do not change any existing test's assertions: the default (not curated) behaviour is unchanged, and tests/test_digest_propose.py must still pass as it is. You can run the listed checks yourself with the run_checks tool before you report; CLIVE runs them again in its own sandbox after you report, and the independent review returns its findings to your next attempt. Do not report an owner decision for GitHub acceptance: it runs automatically after your candidate is published.
acceptance_criteria: with curated, every builder skill of the artifact is proposed and none needs the owner
without curated, behaviour is exactly as before and existing tests pass unchanged
under curated every other target keeps its budget and needs_owner, and a licence that forbids reuse still needs the owner
the --curated flag is passed through both scripts and refused with --self and --no-relate
every listed check passes in the worker's workspace
